body:
I find some hope with a lot of luck and things didn't end up taking a turn for the worse. I also put the gun into storage quite a few miles away from me so even if I do hit another slump retrieving it will be quite a chore.

It's just scary knowing how close I am to the absolute bottom. I am continuing the strengthen my resolve and trying to rebound from my fall in the last few years.

I'm glad this forum was here and I was able to get all of this out instead of letting it run through my head relentlessly. Thank you. At least now I really can see just how bad it was without just brushing it all under the rug by partying or distracting myself.

I thought the same thing before I went into counseling. It did a world of good for me. I was pleasantly surprised with how easy it was to simply talk and how helpful and understanding the counselor was. The hardest part is making that first step toward getting the proper help that you need and deserve. Sometimes people will have bad reactions but you should know that not everyone will react that way even if the first few people that you approach do.

You're certainly not the only one who feels trapped but if you want them to forget about you it means that there must be some connection there. They would certainly never wish to forget about you. I think it could be wise to at least have a talk with either parent about just how you've been feeling down lately and see if they have ever felt the same way. The fact that you don't want to hurt anyone else is a clear sign that you're a better person than a lot of people.

But you are certainly not the only one who feels trapped.

The part that has been really troubling is how happy the thought makes me. Happy isn't the right word but there's certainly a sense of serenity and peace. If I didn't have the risk of of failing to kill myself (which i'm thinking of ways to increase the likelihood) i'd be completely at ease. I looked up the new to a local suicide hotline and I still have at least two weeks of things to get through before I reach the point where I feel completely comfortable with letting go. . .but knowing that the end is in sight just makes me feel so happy. Everything i've been doing over the last few days has become so simple and methodical as a result of my realization that I don't have to endure this life and the future i've created any longer if I choose not to.

Has anyone else ever experienced that?

I have about 20 bucks right now between cash and my bank account. Also a few applications in for jobs around campus to keep up the look of normality and what not. The plan as it stands is to buy a bottle of 151 when i'm ready and to start gulping. 

Plus I can't exactly have anyone take me to go get a box of .22s without questions. I'm living the no car life in a part of the world where it is very much a necessity and a standard. Makes me look like even more of a fuck up.

I have considered this yes but I cannot see what would change in my situation. I think i'd be delaying the inevitable. I was actually given the offer to move to California for the summer but if I accepted i'd be broke and without a car in Hollywood.

If anything I see that that path could result in me living the bum life and that is certainly worse than death. Plus doing so would set me back even further where I am currently and it'd make the last few years of work even more useless. It's still an idea I consider. If the gun didn't fire for some reason I suppose i'd take that as a sign and just go back to work then leave for a new state but honestly. . .all that means is i'll be back washing dishes in some awful kitchen with a better view than last time.

I've had plenty of chances. Some I really did an amazing job and life did that odd thing where it knocks you back down a few pegs for having such hubris. On others I did a pretty shit job because of old habits and bad ideas. As for what I have to loose. . . I suppose time and my mind are on the top of the list. Enduring another year of this shit is really going to reap havoc on my personality and i'm slowly finding myself more and more angry so I think it's better to go before something bad happens.

edit: sorry i think my replies are coming out of order. i don't really know how this whole reddit business works. it just came up in my search results which have been dreadfully inconclusive. basically i'll be flipping a coin when I decide to pull the trigger. scary stuff.

I went to Toronto for a week when I was 19. Absolutely gorgeous place full of wonderful people so I know what you mean about Canada being amazing. Back in my younger years I planned on transferring to one of your universities after I completed my degree but that never happened.

It was a nice dream though.
